/mnt/source/mariadb_cloud_nesono_data/ib_logfile0: file changed while we backed it up
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is as part of the borgmatic backup
I’ll trace how the backup is triggered and how the shutdown script stops the services that write those two files.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run on the production host. All services except Borg are offline during backup.
set -euo pipefail

compose=(docker compose -f /svc/volumes/docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml)
services=()
applications=()
databases=()
restart_needed=false

exec 9>/run/lock/compose-backup.lock
echo 'Waiting for running service jobs or another cold backup to finish...'
flock -x 9

restart_services() {
    echo 'Restarting previously running services...'
    "${compose[@]}" start --wait --wait-timeout 180 "${services[@]}"
}

cleanup() {
    result=$?
    trap - EXIT INT TERM
    if $restart_needed; then
        if ! restart_services; then
            echo 'Restart failed; check docker compose ps and restore services manually.' >&2
            result=1
        fi
    fi
    exit "$result"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

# Verify Borg's existing passphrase file before interrupting services.
"${compose[@]}" exec -T borg-backup sh -ec 'test -r "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE"'
running=$("${compose[@]}" ps --status running --services)
while IFS= read -r service; do
    [[ -n "$service" && "$service" != borg-backup ]] || continue
    services+=("$service")
    # Keep this classification in sync when adding a database service.
    case "$service" in
        mysql_*|mariadb_*|pgsql_*|redis_*) databases+=("$service") ;;
        *) applications+=("$service") ;;
    esac
done <<< "$running"
[[ ${#services[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo 'No running services to back up.' >&2; exit 1; }

restart_needed=true
echo 'Stopping applications, then databases...'
if [[ ${#applications[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    "${compose[@]}" stop --timeout 120 "${applications[@]}"
fi
if [[ ${#databases[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    "${compose[@]}" stop --timeout 120 "${databases[@]}"
fi

# Do not archive a database that was killed after its shutdown timeout.
containers=$("${compose[@]}" ps --all --quiet "${services[@]}")
[[ -n "$containers" ]] || { echo 'Stopped containers not found.' >&2; exit 1; }
while IFS= read -r container; do
    state=$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.OOMKilled}} {{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.service"}}' "$container")
    read -r active status oom service <<< "$state"
    if [[ "$active" != false || "$status" == 137 || "$oom" != false ]]; then
        echo "Container $container did not stop safely ($state); aborting backup." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    case "$service" in
        mysql_*|mariadb_*|pgsql_*|redis_*)
            [[ "$status" == 0 ]] || { echo "$service exited with $status; aborting backup." >&2; exit 1; } ;;
    esac
done <<< "$containers"

echo 'Creating Borg archive...'
"${compose[@]}" exec -T borg-backup sh -ec '
    BORG_PASSPHRASE=$(cat "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE")
    export BORG_PASSPHRASE
    exec borgmatic create --verbosity 1 --stats
'
restart_services
restart_needed=false
echo 'Backup completed; services restarted.'
# Live backup disabled; cold backups run via /usr/local/sbin/backup.sh on the host.
# 0 3 * * * export BORG_PASSPHRASE=$(cat $BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE) && export MAIL_USER=$(cat $BORG_MAIL_USER_FILE) && export MAIL_PASSWORD=$(cat $BORG_MAIL_PASSWORD_FILE) && /scripts/run.sh 2>&1
location:
  source_directories:
    - /mnt/source
  repositories:
    - path: "ssh://u147627@u147627.your-backup.de:23/home/green"
      storage_quota: 950G
  one_file_system: true

storage:
  #   Passphrase is set in variable $BORG_PASSPHRASE
  compression: lz4
  archive_name_format: "backup-{now}"

retention:
  keep_hourly: 24
  keep_daily: 14
  keep_weekly: 2
  keep_monthly: 5
  keep_yearly: 0
  prefix: "backup-"

consistency:
  checks:
    - repository
    - archives
  check_last: 3
  prefix: "backup-"

hooks:
  before_backup:
    - echo "Starting a backup job."
  after_backup:
    - echo "Backup created."
  on_error:
    - echo "Error while creating a backup."
- name: Install root's host schedule and cold-backup script
  hosts: green
  tasks:
    - name: Install cold-backup script
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: roles/compose/files/borgmatic/backup.sh
        dest: /usr/local/sbin/backup.sh
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0750"

    - name: Read current root crontab
      ansible.builtin.command: crontab -u root -l
      register: installed_root_crontab
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: installed_root_crontab.rc not in [0, 1]

    - name: Preserve previous root crontab before replacement
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: "{{ installed_root_crontab.stdout }}\n"
        dest: /root/crontab.before-ansible
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0600"
        backup: true
      when:
        - installed_root_crontab.rc == 0
        - installed_root_crontab.stdout != lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'production/root.crontab')

    - name: Copy reviewed host crontab
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: production/root.crontab
        dest: /usr/local/share/infrastructure-root.crontab
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0600"

    - name: Install reviewed root crontab
      ansible.builtin.command: crontab -u root /usr/local/share/infrastructure-root.crontab
      when: installed_root_crontab.stdout != lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'production/root.crontab')
      changed_when: true
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost/ || exit 1"]
    restart: unless-stopped

  # backup
  borg-backup:
    image: b3vis/borgmatic:msmtp-1.7
    volumes:
      - /svc/volumes:/mnt/source:ro
      - borgmatic_config:/etc/borgmatic.d/
      - borgmatic_keys:/root/.ssh
      - borgmatic_state:/root/.borgmatic
      - borgmatic_borg_config:/root/.config/borg
      - borgmatic_cache:/root/.cache/borg
    environment:
      BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE: /run/secrets/borgmatic_passphrase
      BORG_MAIL_USER_FILE: /run/secrets/robot_mail_user
      BORG_MAIL_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/robot_mail_password
      MAIL_RELAY_HOST: smtp.nesono.com
      MAIL_PORT: 25
      MAIL_FROM: robot@issing.link
      MAIL_TO: n3s0n0@gmail.com
      BORG_RSH: "ssh -p23 -i ~/.ssh/id_ssh_rsa"
      TZ: "UTC"
    secrets:
      - borgmatic_passphrase
      - robot_mail_user
      - robot_mail_password
    entrypoint: >
      /bin/sh -c "export BORG_PASSPHRASE=$$(cat $$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE) &&
      export MAIL_USER=$$(cat $$BORG_MAIL_USER_FILE) && export
      MAIL_PASSWORD=$$(cat $$BORG_MAIL_PASSWORD_FILE) && exec /entry.sh"
    restart: on-failure

  # MySQL database for mail
  mysql_mail:
The former Borgmatic in-container schedule is disabled in this checkout, as
described below. Cold backups can be scheduled separately in root's host
crontab. Avoid overlapping image updates, deployments, and cold backups.

## Backups

[Borgmatic configuration](roles/compose/files/borgmatic/config.yaml) backs up
`/svc/volumes`, mounted read-only at `/mnt/source`, to a Hetzner Storage Box over
SSH port 23. The configuration specifies retention and repository checks.
The passphrase and notification credentials come from Docker secrets.

The backup covers the mounted volume tree, subject to its configured
`one_file_system` boundary. It does not include the controller checkout, root's
crontab, or `/var/docker_compose_secrets`. Keep separate recoverable copies of
those settings and credentials.

### Disabled live-backup schedule

[Borgmatic's crontab](roles/compose/files/borgmatic/crontab.txt) has its former
daily 03:00 UTC live-backup job commented out. Deploy the updated file with
Ansible and restart `borg-backup` to reload its schedule. Until that change is
deployed, the server may still run the live backup, which does not stop
applications or databases.

From the server shell, list archives or run the configured backup:

```sh
dc exec -T borg-backup sh -ec 'export BORG_PASSPHRASE="$(cat "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE")"; exec borgmatic list'
dc exec -T borg-backup sh -ec 'export BORG_PASSPHRASE="$(cat "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE")"; exec borgmatic'
```

For an interactive backup-container shell:

```sh
dc exec borg-backup sh
export BORG_PASSPHRASE="$(cat "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE")"
```

### Cold backups

### Cold backups

Install or update the script from the controller:

```sh
ansible-playbook -i production/hosts green_nesono.yml --tags backup_script
```

Run it as root on the server, keeping the SSH connection open until it finishes:

```sh
/usr/local/sbin/backup.sh
```

The script stops currently running services except Borg, stopping applications
before databases. It aborts if a database was forcibly killed, creates an
archive, and restarts the services that were previously running. Websites,
cloud services, and mail access are unavailable throughout the archive creation.

To run daily at 03:00 host local time (Europe/Berlin), add this optional entry
with `sudo crontab -e`:

```cron
0 3 * * * /usr/local/sbin/backup.sh >> /var/log/compose-backup.log 2>&1
```

This entry is installed by `host_crontab.yml`. Disable the old container schedule
before enabling it. Do not deploy or run service-management commands during
the backup.

The cold-backup script only creates archives. Disabling the old scheduled job
also disables its pruning, compaction, and checks; schedule those separately
without overlapping the cold backup. For a manual maintenance run after the
services have restarted:

```sh
dc exec -T borg-backup sh -ec 'export BORG_PASSPHRASE="$(cat "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE")"; exec borgmatic prune compact check'
```

content.text:
**The warnings came from the old live backup, which is still running alongside the new cold backup.** I matched both warnings to the production Borgmatic container logs for November 21. The host’s cold-backup log shows that its separate run stopped Compose services, created an archive, and restarted them without those warnings.

The host runs `/usr/local/sbin/backup.sh` at **03:00 Berlin time**. The Borgmatic container still has an active crontab running `/scripts/run.sh` at **03:00 UTC**, which was **04:00 Berlin time** that day. By then the services were back online, so Nextcloud could update `audit.log` and MariaDB could update its InnoDB redo log, `ib_logfile0`. The read-only mount prevents Borg from writing to the source, while the running services can still write through their own mounts. [Borg documentation](https://borgbackup.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage/create.html)

I verified that the old job is already commented out in the container’s mounted `crontab.txt`. The active crontab still contains it. The next step is to restart `borg-backup` outside the cold-backup window so it reloads the schedule, then verify that `crontab -l` inside the container has no active `/scripts/run.sh` entry. I left production unchanged. [Repository backup instructions](/Users/iss/Developer/postfix_docker/infrastructure/README.md:276)

For a restore, use the archive from the host’s cold run over the later live archive. The `ib_logfile0` warning means the live archive’s database consistency is unverified.
Where are the changes to the repo here?

I made no repository changes. The old live schedule was already commented out in [crontab.txt](/Users/iss/Developer/postfix_docker/infrastructure/roles/compose/files/borgmatic/crontab.txt:2), and the cold schedule was already defined in [production/root.crontab](/Users/iss/Developer/postfix_docker/infrastructure/production/root.crontab:15).

I traced the warnings to production’s active container crontab, which still had the old entry even though the mounted file had been updated. Production still needs to reload that schedule.

On the production host, as root, run this when no backup is in progress:

```sh
docker compose -f /svc/volumes/docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml restart borg-backup
```

Then check the container’s active crontab:

```sh
docker compose -f /svc/volumes/docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml \
  exec -T borg-backup crontab -l
```

The `0 3 * * * ... /scripts/run.sh` entry should be absent or commented out with `#`. This restarts only `borg-backup`. The cold backup remains scheduled in the host’s root crontab.
Will I get any more emails now? Since you said the backup was running twice, and I only received one message a day

Once the old container cron job is disabled, you should stop receiving the daily backup email. That job ran the image’s mail-enabled `/scripts/run.sh`, which explains why you received one email even though two backups ran.

The host’s cold backup runs `borgmatic create` directly and redirects its output to `/var/log/compose-backup.log`. With the current setup, it sends neither a daily success email nor a failure email.
I would like to get an email, though, since I want to observe the output every day
I’ll add a daily email to the host’s cold-backup script using the existing Borgmatic mail relay. It will include the shutdown, backup, and restart output.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run on the production host. All services except Borg are offline during backup.
set -uo pipefail

compose=(docker compose -f /svc/volumes/docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml)

restart_services() {
    echo 'Restarting previously running services...'
    "${compose[@]}" start --wait --wait-timeout 180 "${services[@]}"
}

cleanup() {
    result=$?
    trap - EXIT INT TERM
    if $restart_needed; then
        if ! restart_services; then
            echo 'Restart failed; check docker compose ps and restore services manually.' >&2
            result=1
        fi
    fi
    exit "$result"
}
run_backup() {
    services=()
    applications=()
    databases=()
    restart_needed=false

    exec 9>/run/lock/compose-backup.lock
    echo 'Waiting for running service jobs or another cold backup to finish...'
    flock -x 9

    trap cleanup EXIT
    trap 'exit 130' INT
    trap 'exit 143' TERM

    # Verify Borg's existing passphrase file before interrupting services.
    "${compose[@]}" exec -T borg-backup sh -ec 'test -r "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE"'
    running=$("${compose[@]}" ps --status running --services)
    while IFS= read -r service; do
        [[ -n "$service" && "$service" != borg-backup ]] || continue
        services+=("$service")
        # Keep this classification in sync when adding a database service.
        case "$service" in
            mysql_*|mariadb_*|pgsql_*|redis_*) databases+=("$service") ;;
            *) applications+=("$service") ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$running"
    [[ ${#services[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo 'No running services to back up.' >&2; exit 1; }

    restart_needed=true
    echo 'Stopping applications, then databases...'
    if [[ ${#applications[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        "${compose[@]}" stop --timeout 120 "${applications[@]}"
    fi
    if [[ ${#databases[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        "${compose[@]}" stop --timeout 120 "${databases[@]}"
    fi

    # Do not archive a database that was killed after its shutdown timeout.
    containers=$("${compose[@]}" ps --all --quiet "${services[@]}")
    [[ -n "$containers" ]] || { echo 'Stopped containers not found.' >&2; exit 1; }
    while IFS= read -r container; do
        state=$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.OOMKilled}} {{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.service"}}' "$container")
        read -r active status oom service <<< "$state"
        if [[ "$active" != false || "$status" == 137 || "$oom" != false ]]; then
            echo "Container $container did not stop safely ($state); aborting backup." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        case "$service" in
            mysql_*|mariadb_*|pgsql_*|redis_*)
                [[ "$status" == 0 ]] || { echo "$service exited with $status; aborting backup." >&2; exit 1; } ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$containers"

    echo 'Creating Borg archive...'
    "${compose[@]}" exec -T borg-backup sh -ec '
        BORG_PASSPHRASE=$(cat "$BORG_PASSPHRASE_FILE")
        export BORG_PASSPHRASE
        exec borgmatic create --verbosity 1 --stats
    '
    restart_services
    restart_needed=false
    echo 'Backup completed; services restarted.'
}

report=$(mktemp) || exit 1
trap 'rm -f -- "$report"' EXIT

# Keep errexit in the backup subprocess and collect both pipeline statuses.
(
    trap - EXIT
    set -e
    run_backup
) 2>&1 | tee "$report"
read -r backup_status report_status <<< "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

subject='Borgmatic cold backup: SUCCESS'
if (( backup_status != 0 || report_status != 0 )); then
    subject='Borgmatic cold backup: FAILED'
fi

if ! "${compose[@]}" exec -T borg-backup sh -ec '
    {
        printf "From: %s\nTo: %s\nSubject: %s\n\n" "$MAIL_FROM" "$MAIL_TO" "$1"
        cat
    } | sendmail -t
' sh "$subject" < "$report"; then
    echo 'Could not send cold-backup report.' >&2
    report_status=1
fi

if (( backup_status != 0 )); then
    exit "$backup_status"
fi
exit "$report_status"
